newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil minister criticizes U.S. trade policy-paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil minister criticizes U.S. trade policy-paper.

text.p: Brazil's Foreign Affairs Minister Luiz Felipe Lampreia criticized the U.S. trade policy by saying the United States has one of the most closed economies in some key sectors for Brazil, local newspapers said.
"The United States has one of the most closed economies in some sectors considered of great importance to our country," Lampreia was quoted as saying by O Globo newspaper.
He cited U.S. restrictions on Brazilian exports of steel, shoes, textile goods and orange juice, the newspaper said.

Although relations between Brazil and the United States have improved significantly in the last years, Lampreia noted trade is the "worrisome and disturbing" issue in relations between the two countries, press reports said.
He said Brazil's trade deficit with the U.S. reached $3.0 billion, more than 50 percent of the country's total deficit in 1996, Gazeta Mercantil newspaper said.
Brazilian imports of U.S. goods jumped to $12 billion from $4.4 billion since the beginning of the 90s, while exports to the U.S. rose to $9.0 billion from $7.6 billion in the period, it added.
